newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply down on policy jitters.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply down on policy jitters.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished sharply lower on Friday as investors dumped shares in the final half-hour amid what brokers called anxiety over privatisation of state firms and central bank inquiries into investment flows.
The weighted index was virtually unchanged through most of the session but turned sharply lower in late trade, ending 165.57 points or 1.95 percent lower at 8,326.53.
Turnover was active at T$136.9 billion, but well below the near-record volumes registered in early April.
"Investors were disappointed by the government policies and, when there was no sight of an upswing, they started dumping shares," said analyst Oliver Fang of Natioanl Securities.
Fang said investors worrid that share prices could be hit by a flood of state bank equity released in what officials said on Wednesday would be an accelerated privatisation scheme.

Another negative factor was the central bank's vow to look more closely at investment flows to ensure Taiwan capital is not being channeled illegally to rival China and that local banks' holdings are not improperly invested in stocks, Fang said.

Beijing's approval on Thursday for six Taiwan shippers to commence direct sailings across the Taiwan strait for the first time since 1949 pushed transport shares up in early trading, but in the end the sector was hit hard, tumbling 2.56 percent.
"Basically, investors had expected that (breakthrough) for some time, and no longer found it inspiring," said analyst Amy Huang of Nomura Securities.
Losses were seen virtually across the board, with plastics falling 2.27 percent, rubber shares 3.65 percent and the hypersensitive electronics sector 4.4 percent.
Brokers expected the index to consolidate in the near term.
